core_insight: Layered architecture is about isolating change by direction of dependency, not about folder structure. Dependencies point inward to stable domain, so UI, business rules, and persistence can evolve independently.

scenes.voice: Why does a clean codebase turn tangled as requirements grow?
scenes.visual: Split screen: clean code on left, tangled wires spreading across controllers, UI, DB on right.

scenes.voice: The real problem isn't mess. It's independent change and ownership. UI changes with UX, business rules change with domain, persistence changes with platform. When mixed, one team blocks another.
scenes.visual: Three timelines moving at different speeds labeled UI, Domain, Persistence, colliding in a mixed codebase.
scenes.on_screen_text: Different concerns change at different speeds

scenes.voice: The obvious fix is separate files. But files don't stop dependencies. The constraint is direction of dependency.
scenes.visual: Folders labeled Presentation, Application, Domain, Infrastructure with arrows going both ways, then red X.

scenes.voice: Layered architecture makes dependencies point inward. Presentation knows Application, Application knows Domain, Domain knows nothing about infrastructure. Infrastructure implements interfaces the domain defines.
scenes.visual: Onion layers with arrows pointing inward.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart TD
    Client --> Pres[Presentation / API]
    Pres --> App[Application / Use Cases]
    App --> Dom[Domain / Business Rules]
    Dom --> Infra[Infrastructure / Data, Messaging, External]
    Pres -.-> Infra

scenes.voice: A request enters Presentation, maps to an application use case, domain enforces invariants, infrastructure persists. Data flows in, control flows out.
scenes.visual: Animated flow: HTTP request down through layers, domain check highlighted, response up.

scenes.voice: This buys independent evolution and testability. UI redesign touches Presentation only. Postgres to DynamoDB touches Infrastructure only. Business rule change touches Domain and Application only.
scenes.visual: Three edits highlighted in separate layers with other layers grayed out.

scenes.voice: The trade-off is indirection and discipline. Each layer adds mapping. Leakage, anemic domain, or circular dependencies defeat the model. You pay for isolation with latency and enforcement.
scenes.visual: Thin layers with small latency arrows, then warning icons for leakage and anemic domain.

scenes.voice: Layered architecture isolates change, not files. Keep dependencies inward.
scenes.visual: Onion diagram with core Domain glowing.

mental_model: Think of the application as an onion. The core domain is most stable and valuable. Outer layers are adapters that change faster. Dependencies only point inward, so the core never knows about the outside. Change is isolated by direction, not by folder.
final_takeaway: Layered architecture exists to isolate change. Dependencies must point inward toward domain.
